turns.t: Hello, doctor. I woke up on Tuesday with a stiff neck, and it's not eased. I suspect I slept on it badly.
That's very common. Which side is it, and what's the movement like?
Right side, running down into the shoulder. I can't turn my head to the right without a sharp pain. Looking left is fine.
Have you any numbness or pins and needles in your arm or hand?
No, nothing in the arm. It's only the neck and a little into the shoulder.
Any injury before, a fall, a car accident, lifting something heavy? ~
No, nothing like that. I did spend the night on my friend's sofa, which has a pillow like a brick. ~
Ah, the sofa. That tends to be the culprit. ~
I did think so. Is it serious? ~
Almost never. Let me check you over to be sure. Temperature first. ~
Of course. ~
Temperature 36.6, pulse 70.
Good. ~
Now I'm going to see how far your neck moves, so tell me where it pinches. Look left.
That's fine. ~
Now over your right shoulder. ~
Ow. That's it. ~
Right, no fever and no worrying signs. This is a muscle strain from the awkward position. ~
How long will it take to settle? ~
Usually three to seven days. It should be a bit better each day. ~
Should I rest it? ~
Not completely. Gentle movement is better than keeping still. A warm pack on the muscle for twenty minutes helps.
I have a wheat bag. ~
Perfect. Use one pillow that keeps your neck level, not two. ~
I'll get rid of the brick. ~
Take care with sudden movements, and avoid carrying a heavy bag on that shoulder. ~
And should I come back? ~
Only if it's still bad after a week, or if you get weakness or numbness in the arm, a fever, or a severe headache.
Understood. Thank you. ~
Hope the neck loosens up. ~
